chapter.title: What an agent is, and what it is not

cards.body: A clipping service is a person, not a magic box. Every morning at 7 an alarm wakes them, they pick up the same 5 newspapers, read them, cut out the stories about your rivals, and leave one short note on your desk. An agent is that person, done by a program. The alarm, the papers, the reader and the note are its 4 parts.

cards.title: The 4 boxes
cards.body:
An agent is a program that runs on its own, without you pressing a button, and uses an AI model to read and write text. That is the whole definition. Everything else is detail.

Box 1 is the trigger. The trigger is the alarm clock: a rule that says start now, for example every day at 7am. Without it, nothing happens until you remember to run it.

Box 2 is the sources. Sources are the newspapers: the exact web pages the agent will open, like a rival's pricing page. The agent only knows what is on those pages. It does not know anything else about your rivals.

Box 3 is the model. The model is the reader: an AI system, like Claude, that takes in text and writes text back. You hand it the page text and an instruction, and it hands you a few sentences.

Box 4 is the output. The output is the note on your desk: an email, a chat message or a file where the summary lands. If the note never reaches you, the agent did nothing useful.

Draw the 4 boxes left to right with arrows between them. Trigger starts it, sources feed it, the model reads, the output delivers. That drawing is the whole plan for the next 6 chapters.

cards.prompt: Your friend says they built a competitor-tracking agent. Every Monday they open a chat window, paste in a rival's pricing page, and ask the AI what changed. Which box is missing?

whyNot.a: That's the reader, and it is there: the AI in the chat window is the model.
whyNot.c: That's the newspapers, and they are there: the pasted pricing page is the source.

cards.reteach: The trigger is the part that starts the work without a person. If your friend has to remember to open the chat on Monday, your friend is the alarm clock. An agent has its own alarm, so it runs even on the Monday you forget.

cards.title: One morning, box by box
cards.body: Say you sell a scheduling app and you watch 3 rivals. At 7:00 the trigger fires. The agent opens 3 pricing pages and 2 changelog pages, 5 sources in total, and pulls the text off each. It hands that text to the model with one instruction: say what changed in 2 sentences and quote the line it came from. At 7:04 the output lands in your inbox: Rival B raised its Team plan from $12 to $15 per seat, source: pricing page, line 'Team: $15/seat/month'. You never touched a keyboard.

cards.title: What an agent is not
cards.body:
An agent is not a chatbot. A chatbot waits for you to type. An agent runs when the trigger says so, and you read the result later, often hours later.

The model is not the agent. The model is one box of four. It cannot open a web page, remember yesterday, or send an email by itself. The other 3 boxes do that work, and you will build them with ordinary code, not with AI.

An agent does not know anything you did not give it. If a rival announces a price cut on a page you did not list as a source, the agent will not see it. This is a feature: it means every line in the note can be traced to a page you chose.

cards.prompt: You want the agent to tell you when a rival hires a sales lead. Which change applies the 4-box idea correctly?

options.text: Add the rival's careers page to the sources
Tell the model to also check for hires, and leave the sources as they are
Make the trigger run every hour instead of every day

whyNot.b: That's the reader, not the newspapers: the model can only read pages it is handed, so a new instruction with no new page finds nothing.
whyNot.c: That's the alarm clock, not the newspapers: running more often re-reads the same pages, which still do not mention hires.

cards.reteach: The agent sees exactly the pages in its sources box and nothing more. If you want it to notice something new, the first question is always: which page would that appear on? Add that page. Then the model has something to read.

cards.body: The common mistake is treating the model as if it were the whole agent, and asking it what your competitors are doing with no sources attached. It will answer with confidence, from old training data or from nothing. Spot it fast: if a claim in the note has no page it came from, the model guessed.

cards.prompt: Which of these is the definition of an agent that this chapter uses?

options.text: An AI model that is smarter than a chatbot
A program that runs on its own on a schedule and uses a model to read and write text
A tool that downloads web pages and saves them

whyNot.a: That's the model box on its own, the reader: a model is one part of an agent, not a smarter version of one.
whyNot.c: That's the sources box plus a download step: fetching pages is one part, with no reader and no note.

cards.reteach: Four boxes: trigger, sources, model, output. Take any one away and it stops being an agent. A model alone is a chatbot. A downloader alone is a scraper. Together, on a schedule, with a note at the end, it is an agent.

cards.body: Tonight, on paper, draw 4 boxes in a row: trigger, sources, model, output. Under sources, write 1 rival and the one page of theirs you would most want read every morning.

chapter.outcomeLine: You can now draw the 4 boxes of a competitor-tracking agent and say what each one does.
